subject: Follow-up: deployment tenancy & SLOs for Acme AI PoC
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme-ai.com>; Samir Desai <samir@indusware.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: deployment tenancy & SLOs for Acme AI PoC

Hi Lena / Samir —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum for the PoC: 

Recap from our conversation:
- Goal: 3-week PoC to validate latency at p50/p95 for your realtime assistant, and measure cost per 1K tokens.
- Workloads: mix of short queries (~16 tokens) and long-context summarization (~2k tokens).
- Primary concerns you flagged: tenant isolation (noisy neighbor risk), predictable p95 latency, and data residency for logs.

Clarifications / options we covered:
1) Hosted API (fastest to start): shared routing across tenants but with hard SLOs; we can pin an edition with higher priority routing to reduce interference. Not guaranteed single-tenant hardware.
2) Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool for only your workloads (single-tenant), predictable throughput and lower variance on p95, monthly reservation required.
3) Private VPC (customer-managed): control plane in your VPC or on-prem bundle; full isolation, audit/log forwarding to your SIEM.

Proposed next steps:
- You: confirm which SLO tradeoffs are acceptable (is a soft p95 SLO with 99.9% uptime ok, or do you need strict p95 SLA backed by dedicated capacity?).
- Me: share a short comparison doc and a quick pricing delta table (attached).
- Ops: if you want Dedicated or Private, send a short list of compliance controls to validate (SOC2, data retention, KMS).

Attachments: poC-deployment-options.xlsx (delta pricing + config), redwood-dedicated-security-faq.pdf

If helpful, I can schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive with Monica and Marissa next week to go over KV caching, autoscaling burst behavior, and expected p95 numbers on dedicated pools.

Best,
Jordan

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
+jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme-ai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme-ai.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment tenancy & SLOs for Acme AI PoC

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear summary. A couple of quick answers from our side: 
- For the PoC we want to prove p95 <= 250ms for short queries and p95 <= 1s for long-context flows. If shared hosting shows variance outside that margin, we will need to move to Dedicated for production.
- Data residency: logs must be retained in our account for 180 days and we need a path to deliver audit logs to our SIEM.
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II required for production; PoC can run on Hosted if the isolation guarantees are documented.

Can you include an explicit note in the comparison doc on the mitigations for noisy neighbor scenarios (e.g., request throttling, tenant-priority queueing, KV cache warmup behavior)?

Lena
Director, Product
Acme AI

Date: Mon, 24 May 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment tenancy & SLOs for Acme AI PoC

Lena —

Thanks — attached is an annotated one-pager that calls out specific noisy-neighbor mitigations and what we can commit to for the PoC vs production. Highlights: 
- PoC (Hosted): isolated priority lanes, token throttles per-tenant, aggressive KV prefix caching for your session patterns. These reduce p95 variance but do not guarantee single-tenant hardware.
- Production (Dedicated): reserved pool with hard isolation, configurable autoscaling policy, and reserved capacity for burst windows. Expected p95 variance < 8% on long tails based on similar workloads.
- Private VPC: full control plane in your network, KMS integration, and log export; recommended if you need on-prem audit controls.

I've also included a short logistics checklist for SOC 2 evidence you requested. Let me know if you want that routed to your procurement contact as a formal pack.

Proposed times for a technical deep-dive (30 min): Wed 5/27 10:00 or Thu 5/28 11:00 (PST). Which works?

Jordan

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-security-faq.pdf, poC-deployment-options.xlsx

Following Jordan's scheduling attempt, I'll run the technical deep-dive and demo a short synthetic test that shows p95 behavior across Shared vs Dedicated setups. Agenda (30 min):
- 5m: architecture overview (routing, queueing, and KV cache)
- 10m: synthetic spike test results (shared tenant under load)
- 10m: dedicated pool behavior and autoscale mechanics
- 5m: Q&A and next steps (SOC 2 evidence handoff)

Prep request: please share a sample E2E request pattern (typical prompt length distribution) and an IP range for whitelisting if we run dedicated PoC nodes in your VPC.
